sites.name: Apollo 11 — Tranquility Base
sites.description: First crewed lunar landing, in southwestern Mare Tranquillitatis. Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21.5 hours on the surface.

sites.name: Apollo 12 — Ocean of Storms
sites.description: Second crewed landing, a precision touchdown near the Surveyor 3 lander in Oceanus Procellarum.

sites.name: Apollo 14 — Fra Mauro
sites.description: Crewed landing in the Fra Mauro highlands, the intended Apollo 13 target; Shepard and Mitchell sampled Cone crater ejecta.

sites.name: Apollo 15 — Hadley–Apennine
sites.description: First J-mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle, landed between Hadley Rille and the Apennine mountains.

sites.name: Apollo 16 — Descartes Highlands
sites.description: Only crewed landing in the lunar central highlands, near Descartes crater.

sites.name: Apollo 17 — Taurus–Littrow
sites.description: Last crewed lunar landing, in the Taurus–Littrow valley; included geologist Harrison Schmitt.

sites.name: Luna 9
sites.description: First spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon and transmit surface images, in Oceanus Procellarum. NSSDCA gives only an approximate position (7.08 N, 64.37 W); the lander has not been unambiguously identified in LRO images.

sites.name: Luna 13
sites.description: Soviet soft lander in Oceanus Procellarum that deployed a soil-mechanics probe and imaged the surface. Position is approximate (TASS communique, as quoted by NSSDCA).

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.description: First robotic sample-return mission from the Moon, landing in Mare Fecunditatis and returning 101 g of regolith.

sites.name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
sites.description: Delivered Lunokhod 1, the first robotic rover on another world, to Mare Imbrium near Sinus Iridum.

sites.name: Luna 20
sites.description: Soviet sample-return lander in the Apollonius highlands between Mare Fecunditatis and Mare Crisium. Position from NSSDCA; the landing time (19:19 UTC) is not stated by NSSDCA and comes from secondary sources.

sites.name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
sites.description: Delivered Lunokhod 2 to Le Monnier crater at the eastern edge of Mare Serenitatis; the rover drove about 39 km.

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.description: Last Soviet lunar mission; returned a 170 g core sample from Mare Crisium. Position from NSSDCA; the landing time (06:36 UTC) comes from secondary sources, NSSDCA does not state it.

sites.name: Luna 25 (crash site)
sites.description: Russia's Luna-25 lost control during a descent orbit change and crashed near Pontécoulant G crater; the impact crater was imaged by LRO.

sites.name: Surveyor 1
sites.description: First US soft landing on the Moon, in a flooded crater in Oceanus Procellarum.

sites.name: Surveyor 3
sites.description: Landed in a crater in Oceanus Procellarum; parts were retrieved by Apollo 12 astronauts in 1969.

sites.name: Surveyor 5
sites.description: Landed in Mare Tranquillitatis and performed the first in-situ chemical analysis of lunar soil with an alpha-scattering instrument.

sites.name: Surveyor 6
sites.description: Landed in Sinus Medii and performed the first liftoff from the lunar surface (a 'hop').

sites.name: Surveyor 7
sites.description: Last Surveyor; landed on the ejecta blanket north of Tycho crater in the southern highlands.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 / Yutu
sites.description: First Chinese soft landing; landed in northern Mare Imbrium and deployed the Yutu rover. Position from LROC NAC (44.1214 N, 340.4884 E); landing time 21:11 Beijing time per Xinhua/CNSA reports.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2
sites.description: First soft landing on the lunar far side, in Von Karman crater within the South Pole-Aitken basin. Landing time 10:26 Beijing time (02:26 UTC) per Chinese state-media reports.

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.description: Sample-return mission that landed near Mons Rümker in Oceanus Procellarum and returned about 1.73 kg of samples.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.description: First far-side sample return, from Apollo basin inside the South Pole-Aitken basin. Landing 06:23 Beijing time on 2 June 2024 (CNSA/Xinhua) = 22:23 UTC on 1 June.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 — Shiv Shakti Point
sites.description: India's first lunar soft landing, near the south pole; Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. The landing point is named Shiv Shakti. Time (12:33 UTC) from NSSDCA entry 2023-098A.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram (crash site)
sites.description: Vikram lost contact about 2 km above the surface during powered descent and impacted near Manzinus craters; wreckage was identified in LRO images (LROC). The time of signal loss (about 20:23 UTC) is approximate, not an official ISRO timestamp.

sites.name: SLIM — Moon Sniper
sites.description: Japan's precision lander touched down near Shioli crater; it ended up on its nose after losing a main-engine nozzle.

sites.name: Beresheet (crash site)
sites.description: First privately funded lunar lander; its main engine failed during descent and it crashed in Mare Serenitatis. Position is the LROC darkest-pixel location (95% confidence about 20 m x 8 m); the time is approximate, from press reports (about 19:23 UTC).

sites.name: Hakuto-R Mission 1 (crash site)
sites.description: ispace's first lander crashed in Atlas crater after an altitude-estimation error during descent; imaged by LRO.

sites.name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 Resilience (crash site)
sites.description: ispace's Resilience lander made a hard landing in Mare Frigoris on 5 June 2025 (18:13 UTC); LROC located the impact smudge at 60.4445 N, 355.4120 E.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus — Malapert A
sites.description: First US lander since Apollo and first commercial soft landing; touched down near Malapert A and tipped onto its side. Landing time 6:23 pm EST (23:23 UTC) per NASA APOD.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena — Mons Mouton
sites.description: Athena landed in a 20 m crater near the centre of Mons Mouton, about 400 m short of its target, and ended up on its side. Touchdown at about 11:30 am CST (17:30 UTC); NASA gives only an approximate time.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 — Mare Crisium
sites.description: First fully successful commercial lunar landing, in Mare Crisium about 4 km from Mons Latreille. Landed 3:34 am EST (08:34 UTC) per NASA; the NSSDCA entry lists 08:45 UT.

sites.name: VIPER planned destination — Mons Mouton region
sites.description: VIPER was cancelled in July 2024, then re-manifested: on 19 Sep 2025 NASA announced it will be delivered to Mons Mouton by a Blue Origin Blue Moon MK-1 lander (CLPS task order CS-7). Point is the LROC Mons Mouton (Leibnitz Beta Plateau) region centre, not a landing point.

sites.name: IM-3 / Lunar Vertex — Reiner Gamma
sites.description: Planned CLPS lander on the Reiner Gamma swirl in Oceanus Procellarum, carrying the Lunar Vertex magnetic-anomaly investigation. Coordinates are the IAU feature centre.

sites.name: Lunar-VISE — Gruithuisen Domes
sites.description: Planned CLPS delivery of the Lunar-VISE instrument suite to the Gruithuisen silicic volcanic domes. Coordinates are the IAU centre of Gruithuisen Gamma.

sites.name: Draper/ispace APEX 1.0 — Schrödinger Basin
sites.description: Planned CLPS far-side lander (CP-12) to Schrödinger basin. Coordinates are the IAU basin centre, not a published landing point.

sites.name: Haworth (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the LROC NAC mosaic centre of the region, not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: Mons Mouton (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found. Centre is the LROC Leibnitz Beta Plateau (Mons Mouton) value.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1 (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2 (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). Coordinates are the centre of a ~15 x 15 km region (LROC NAC mosaic table, Henriksen et al.), not a landing point. NASA's ninth region, Slater Plain, is not listed because no published centre was found.

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.description: One of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 28 Oct 2024). UNVERIFIED position: the region centre was not found in any primary source opened (it is absent from the LROC region table); value carried over from the earlier catalog. Not a landing point.

sites.name: Shackleton connecting ridge (high-illumination point)
sites.description: Connecting Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters, with near-continuous sunlight. Coordinates are the LROC NAC mosaic region centre (Henriksen et al., Table 1), not a surveyed point.

sites.name: Shackleton rim (SR1)
sites.description: Point on the Shackleton crater rim with long sunlight duration. UNVERIFIED: coordinates carried over from an earlier catalog attributed to De Rosa et al. (2012, Planet. Space Sci. 74, doi in source); the paper's table could not be opened, so treat as approximate.

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.description: Illuminated peak near Shackleton crater. Coordinates are the LROC NAC mosaic region centre (Henriksen et al., Table 1), not a surveyed point.

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor
sites.description: Floor of the 21 km-wide Shackleton crater at the south pole; permanently shadowed cold trap. Coordinates are the IAU crater centre.

sites.name: de Gerlache rim
sites.description: Illuminated point on the rim of de Gerlache crater. UNVERIFIED: coordinates carried over from an earlier catalog attributed to De Rosa et al. (2012, Planet. Space Sci. 74, doi in source); the paper's table could not be opened, so treat as approximate.

sites.name: Malapert peak
sites.description: High peak on the Malapert massif with near-continuous Earth visibility and long sunlight. UNVERIFIED: coordinates carried over from an earlier catalog attributed to De Rosa et al. (2012, Planet. Space Sci. 74, doi in source); the paper's table could not be opened, so treat as approximate.

sites.name: Lunar south pole
sites.description: Rotational south pole of the Moon.

sites.name: Lunar north pole
sites.description: Rotational north pole of the Moon.

sites.name: Peary crater
sites.description: Large crater near the north pole with near-permanently illuminated rim areas. Coordinates are the IAU crater centre.

sites.name: Tycho crater
sites.description: Young 85 km ray crater in the southern highlands with a prominent central peak. Coordinates are the IAU crater centre.

sites.name: Copernicus crater
sites.description: 93 km Copernican-age impact crater near Mare Imbrium with terraced walls and central peaks.

sites.name: Aristarchus plateau
sites.description: Aristarchus crater (40 km) on the volcanic plateau, one of the brightest large near-side craters.

sites.name: Mare Orientale (basin centre)
sites.description: Centre of the 930 km multi-ring Orientale impact basin on the western limb.

sites.name: Far-side centre
sites.description: Point on the equator opposite the sub-Earth point; never visible from Earth and shielded from Earth radio emissions.

sites.name: Sub-Earth point
sites.description: Point where the mean Earth direction crosses the surface (0 N, 0 E), the lunar prime meridian.

sites.name: Marius Hills pit
sites.description: Skylight pit into a possible lava tube in the Marius Hills volcanic complex, Oceanus Procellarum.

sites.name: Tsiolkovskiy crater
sites.description: Far-side crater (180 km) with a prominent central peak and a mare-filled floor.

sites.name: South Pole–Aitken basin centre
sites.description: Approximate centre of the largest and oldest confirmed lunar impact basin (about 2500 km across).
